summary: Taiwan's story is the AI chip boom. On Oct 15 TSMC reported Q3 revenue of $46.72 billion, up 41.2%, a 66.4% gross margin, a Q4 guide of $52.3 to $54.3 billion, and raised 2026 growth to about 44%, saying AI demand is far above supply. Its shares still fell about 2% and the Taiex had its sixth biggest point drop ever, with record net foreign selling of NT$302.56 billion, as global investors cut AI exposure on rate and debt fears. The main local risks remain China-Taiwan tension or US chip tariffs; no new tension was found this week.
for_you: Taiwan is the AI factory. TSMC sales are still growing over 50% a year, which supports NVDA, AMD and the whole AI compute theme. TSMC reports Thursday Oct 15: avoid opening new AI chip swings before that call, and use any post earnings dip in NVDA (Buy zone now) as a long term entry.

changes.what: TSMC reported September sales of NT$511.9 billion, up 54.6% from a year ago, and record Q3 sales of NT$1.494 trillion, above the NT$1.46 trillion LSEG estimate. AI chip demand is still rising.

The Taiex fell 1.95% to 48,341 on Oct 13 as foreign investors sold a net NT$165 billion, the third largest foreign sale on record, after the US chip selloff and Korea's crash. TSMC fell 1.97% to NT$2,490 two days before its results.
changes.for_you: EWT dropped off the Setups list; no swing until after TSMC reports. The call is 2:00pm Taipei time Thursday, which is 2:00am ET. TSM is left out of the bearish list because its sales are still up over 50%; this is foreign money leaving, not a business change.

changes.what: TSMC beat and raised (Q3 revenue $46.72 billion, gross margin 66.4%, 2026 growth now about 44%, capex unchanged at $60 to $64 billion), yet its shares fell about 2% and the Taiex had its sixth steepest point drop with a record NT$302.56 billion of net foreign selling on Oct 15.
changes.for_you: No chip swings yet. TSM's business is fine, so it stays bullish on fundamentals, but it has no buy zone verdict. EWT is hurt by foreign selling. NVDA and AMD are left out: TSMC's demand comments help them, but they fell with the group premarket.

changes.what: The Taiex fell 0.6%, or 289 points, to 46,822 on Oct 19 after the Philadelphia chip index dropped 3.8% on Friday; TSMC closed flat at NT$2,420 (Focus Taiwan via Ad-hoc News).
changes.for_you: No action. TSM (412.61 Friday) holding flat while the index fell is a small sign of relative strength, but it has no buy zone verdict. EWT (106.26) had up/down volume 0.79 on Friday, so sellers still lead.
